output.brief: The rise in cancellations is mainly an accounting-sync problem, not a pricing problem. Since Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March, the connector has silently dropped or doubled invoices. 1,212 of 1,900 Quillbook accounts were affected, and 34% of them cancelled, against 8% of those with no failures. Quillbook accounts churn at about 6% a month whether they are on the new price or the Founders lock. Accounts with no connector show no real change (about 1.9%), at any seat size. The apparent link between price and size of increase arises because larger accounts are more likely to use Quillbook. The Tallymarsh data is too small to show an effect, and its log has not been reviewed. Seasonality and the mobile release do not fit. I'm fairly confident, though the Quillbook fix is not yet scheduled. Next steps: make the Quillbook move to the new interface the top engineering priority, with a fix in three to four weeks. Contact every Quillbook account, including those that cancelled, to correct invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold. Don't roll back the price, and don't start the Tallymarsh rebuild until its log has been reviewed. Count WARN events on the health panel.
